- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots → cap forecast at +10% above recent high or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model underestimates downward moves → add 2–3% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility → smooth 30d forecast with 7-day rolling average to reduce noise.
- When sentiment turns negative after a rally, model fails to adjust → reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment drops below -0.30.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model ignores trend → align forecast with 14-day SMA instead of 30d trend.
- Model often ignores sentiment in early days of forecast horizon → apply sentiment multiplier (e.g., +0.10 to forecast if sentiment > 0.10, -0.10 if < -0.10) for first 7 days.
